questions.question: Draw a cross-section of Earth and label the four layers: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
Use color or labels to show which layers are solid and which are liquid.
Show how the crust is different under the ocean and under a continent.
Sketch convection currents in the mantle. Use arrows to show where material rises and sinks.
Draw Earth's magnetic field. Label the layer that helps create it.
Draw a divergent boundary. Use arrows for plate movement and label what forms.
Draw an ocean plate meeting a continental plate. Label the trench and the volcanoes.
Draw two continental plates colliding. What landform forms?
Draw a transform boundary with arrows for plate movement. Add a star where earthquakes happen.
Draw an earthquake and label the focus and the epicenter.
Draw the water cycle. Label evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
Show where the energy for the water cycle comes from.
Add transpiration, runoff and groundwater to your water cycle.
Draw a mountain where one side gets lots of rain and the other side is dry. Explain with arrows.
Draw the rock cycle. Label igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rock and the processes that connect them.
Show how an igneous rock can become a sedimentary rock.
Draw layers of sedimentary rock. Label the oldest layer.
Draw where heat and pressure make metamorphic rock.
Sketch magma cooling slowly underground and quickly at the surface. Show the crystal sizes.
Draw a cold front from the side. Show the warm air, cold air and where storms form.
Draw a warm front from the side.
Draw a high pressure and a low pressure system. Use arrows for the wind.
Draw how air moves in a sea breeze on a sunny afternoon.
Place Earth at the right spot in its orbit for each season in the northern hemisphere. Then draw an arrow showing which way Earth’s axis tilts.
Drag each label onto the layer of Earth it names. Then draw an arrow to the hottest layer.
Place each moon where it is in its orbit when we see that phase from Earth. The Sun’s light comes from the left.
Put an arrow on each plate and turn it to show how the plates move at a convergent boundary: the plates move toward each other. Then draw what you might see at the surface.
Put an arrow on each plate and turn it to show how the plates move at a divergent boundary: the plates move away from each other. Then draw what you might see at the surface.
Put an arrow on each plate and turn it to show how the plates move at a transform boundary: the plates slide past each other. Then draw what you might see at the surface.

Land or water?
A continent is a very large piece of land. An ocean is a very large body of salt water.
Drop each name in the right lane.

Word match.
You will use these words all lesson: coastline, fossil, mountain chain, evidence.
Drop each meaning or example in the lane for its word.

cards.text: Where the land meets the ocean
The edge of Africa on a map
A print or remains of a plant or animal from long ago
A bone turned to stone inside a rock
Clues that help show something is true
What a scientist uses to support an idea

questions.question:
Look at the map. These are two continents.
Trace the two coastlines that face each other. Use a bright color.

Sentence frame: The two coastlines look ______.

Make a puzzle. Move the two continents. Fit their coastlines together.
Tap a continent. You can turn it. Then draw a circle where the coastlines touch.

Sentence frame: The two continents fit like ______.

What kind of clue is it?
Alfred Wegener used four kinds of evidence.
Drop each clue in the right lane.

cards.text: Africa and South America fit like puzzle pieces
The two coasts have matching curves
Mesosaurus fossils in Africa and South America
Glossopteris plant fossils on many continents
The Appalachians match mountains in Scotland
One long mountain chain, split by an ocean
Glacier scratches in hot places like India
The same rock types on both sides of an ocean

questions.question:
Fossil clue. Mesosaurus was a small reptile. It lived in rivers and lakes. It could not swim across a salty ocean.
Its fossils are in Africa and South America.
Draw an X on each continent where the fossils were found.

Sentence frame: Mesosaurus fossils are on both continents because ______.

Mountain clue. Mountains in the south of Africa match mountains in the south of South America.
This map shows the continents joined. Draw one long mountain chain across both continents. Use ^ ^ ^ for mountains.

Sentence frame: The mountains match because ______.

How did they move? Long ago the continents were joined, like this map. Today they are apart.
Put an arrow on each continent. Turn each arrow to show which way the continent moved.

Sentence frame: The two continents moved ______ from each other.

Wegener’s big idea. In 1912, Wegener said the continents were once joined. Then they drifted apart. To drift is to move slowly.
Many scientists said, “No!” Sort what Wegener had and what he did not have.

cards.text: The same fossils on two continents
An answer for how continents move
A force strong enough to move land
A way to measure the moving land

questions.question:
Make a hypothesis. A hypothesis is a smart guess.
Wegener could not explain how a continent moves. What could push or pull a continent?
Draw your idea and label it. There is no wrong answer.

Sentence frame: I think the continents move because ______.

Build a good answer. A claim is what you think is true. Evidence is a clue. Reasoning explains why the clue proves the claim.
Drop each sentence in the right lane.

cards.text: I think Wegener was right about the continents.
Wegener was wrong. The continents did not move.
Mesosaurus fossils are in Africa and South America.
The coastlines of the two continents fit together.
Glacier scratches are in warm places like India.
Mesosaurus could not swim an ocean, so the land was joined.
Coasts that fit show the land was once one piece.
Glaciers need cold, so India was once in a cold place.

questions.question:
Your decision. Was Wegener right that the continents moved? Use two clues.
Claim: I think Wegener was (right / wrong) because ______.
Evidence: One clue is ______. It was found on ______ and ______.
Reasoning: This shows the continents moved because ______.

Challenge. The continents still move today. They move about as fast as your fingernails grow.
Draw where you think Africa and South America will be in 50 million years. Use arrows.

Sentence frame: In 50 million years, the Atlantic Ocean will be ______ because ______.

Draw a simple circuit with a battery, a switch and a bulb.

Graph y = 2x + 1.
Draw fraction bars to model 3/4 + 1/2.
